extracted.intended_audience: readers of entertainment journalism; podcast listeners and Marc Maron fans
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting a short list of 'must-listen' episodes from a long-running interview podcast by weighing emotional resonance, cultural importance, guest notability, and memorable moments. The page is a magazine-style best-of listicle focused on Marc Maron's WTF episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional depth / balance of heartbreak and humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose conversations that are both heartbreaking and hilarious — episodes that move listeners emotionally while still delivering comedic moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explicitly describes the selections as 'must-listen conversations — both heartbreaking and hilarious.' Examples include the Robin Williams episode (insecurity and suicide) and Ariana Grande (real and confronting death).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural or historical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor episodes that have cultural or historical import either for the podcast or more broadly (moments tied to a presidency, recordings inducted into archives, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Obama interview is described as 'one of the essential texts in WTF history and of the Obama presidency'; the Robin Williams episode was 'inducted into the National Recording Registry at the Library of Congress.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable / A-list guests
rubrics_metrics.description: Include episodes featuring high-profile, widely recognized guests whose presence alone makes the conversation notable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: President Barack Obama, Brad Pitt & Leonardo DiCaprio, Ariana Grande — guest star power is used as a selection factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable / controversial moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Select episodes that contain standout, newsworthy or contentious moments that stick with listeners (on-air walk-offs, unexpected security visits, heated exchanges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gallagher episode features the first-ever WTF 'walk-off' after homophobic and racist remarks; the Obama episode prompted a Secret Service visit to Maron's house—these moments are highlighted as reasons to include episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host/guest vulnerability and candidness
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize interviews where guests (and sometimes the host) open up personally, revealing anxieties, grief, or intimate details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lynn Shelton's 'blind date' interview doubles as a portrait of the filmmaker; Andrew Garfield 'opens up about career anxieties and losing his mother'; Ariana Grande tries to get 'even realer.' The page values candid, intimate conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and diversity of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Showcase the podcast's breadth by including interviews across different fields — music, film, science, activism — demonstrating diverse interests and guests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list ranges from primatologist Jane Goodall to R&B singer Mavis Staples to filmmakers and actors, cited as evidence of Maron's 'diverse interests.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-defining or career-impacting conversations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include episodes that are notable landmarks in a guest's or the host's career — conversations that influenced public perception or a career trajectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mavis Staples episode is 'regarded as one of WTF‘s best conversations'; Andrew Garfield's episode is credited with tracing his 'Garfieldnaissance.' Lorne Michaels' unusually generous time is framed as significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview craft: eliciting rare access or responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Value episodes in which the host secures unusually open, extended, or rare commentary from guests who typically don't give much access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lorne Michaels entry notes Michaels 'so rarely (read: never) gives this much of his time,' suggesting that obtaining such access is a criterion for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising revelations or unexpected content
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose conversations that produce surprising statements or unexpected tangents that make the episode distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jane Goodall 'low-key suggests that Bigfoot is real' — the article highlights such surprising moments as part of what makes an episode essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative of the host's legacy/pioneering status
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick episodes that collectively demonstrate why the host helped 'pioneer the medium' and define their long-running show's legacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames the list as highlights from '1600+ episodes over 16 years' and positions the selections as examples of Maron's contribution to podcasting, implying legacy-representative episodes are criteria.
